questions.stem: The velocity of an engine-powered boat with the current is $15\text{ kmh}^{-1}$ and against the current is $5\text{ kmh}^{-1}$. In a river of width $5\text{ km}$, a boatman starts from point $A$ in order to reach point $B$ straight across on the other bank. From point $C$, at a distance $5\text{ km}$ from point $B$, another person starts moving at the same time with a velocity of $4\text{ kmh}^{-1}$ towards point $B$.

parts.prompt: At what angle had the boatman set off in order to reach point $B$?
parts.answer:
velocity of the boat with the current = $15\text{ kmh}^{-1}$
$$\therefore v + u = 15 \dots\dots\ (i)$$ Similarly, the velocity of the boat against the current = $5\text{ kmh}^{-1}$
$$\therefore v - u = 5 \dots\dots\ (ii)$$
 From $\ (i) +\ (ii)$ we get, $2v = 20$
$$\therefore v = \frac{20}{2}$$

$$v = 10\text{ kmh}^{-1}$$ Again, from $\ (i)$ we get, $u = 15 - v = 15 - 10 = 5\text{ kmh}^{-1}$ reaching point $B$ straight across on the other bank from $A$ `[reaching]`, the resultant angle will be $\theta = 90^\circ$. Let the boatman set off at an angle $\alpha$ with the current in order to reach point $B$.
$\therefore$ direction of the resultant velocity of the boat, $\tan\theta = \frac{v\sin\alpha}{u + v\cos\alpha}$ or, $\tan 90^\circ = \frac{10\sin\alpha}{5 + 10\cos\alpha}$ or, $\frac{1}{\tan 90^\circ} = \frac{5 + 10\cos\alpha}{10\sin\alpha}$ or, $5 + 10\cos\alpha = 0 \left[\because \frac{1}{\tan 90^\circ} = 0\right]$
$\therefore \alpha = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{-5}{10}\right) = 120^\circ\text{ Ans.}$

parts.prompt: Analyse mathematically whether the boatman met the other person when he reached point $B$.
parts.answer:
From (c) we get, in order to go from point $A$ to point $B$ on the other bank, the boatman had rowed the boat at an angle $120^\circ$ with the current.
$\therefore$ the time required by the boatman to reach point $B$ on the other bank,
$$t = \frac{d}{v\sin\alpha}$$

$$t = \frac{5}{10\sin 120^\circ}$$

$$t = 0.577\text{ hr}$$
 Now, if the other person can reach point $B$ in that time from point $C$, a distance $5\text{ km}$ from point $B$, then it is possible for them to meet. If the time required for the other person to reach point $B$ is $t'$, then
$$t' = \frac{s}{v'}$$

$$t' = \frac{5}{4}$$

$$t' = 1.25\text{ hr}$$
 Thus, it is seen that $t' > t$ That is, the boatman had already reached point $B$ before the other person arrived at point $B$. In that case, if the boatman waits a further $(1.25 - 0.577) = 0.67\text{ hr}$ or $(0.67 \times 60) = 40$ minutes after reaching point $B$, he will meet the other person. But if the boatman sets off for some other destination before $40$ minutes have passed, he will not meet the other person.

A at the bottom, B directly opposite on the upper bank. From A, the current $u$ flows to the right, the boat's velocity $v$ points to the upper left, and the resultant velocity is straight up along AB. The angle between the resultant and the current is $\theta=90^\circ$. This is the situation of the shortest path. Now, to cross the river in the minimum time the boat's velocity must be along the width of the river, i.e. $\alpha=90^\circ$. ∴ the time required in this case, $$t_2=\frac{d}{v\sin\alpha}$$ $$t_2 = \frac{1357.648}{7\sin90^\circ}\ \mathrm s$$ $$t_2 = 193.950\ \mathrm s$$ which is less than $t_1$. and the resultant velocity,
$$\begin{aligned} w&=\sqrt{u^2+v^2+2uv\cos\alpha}\\ &=\sqrt{(\sqrt{17})^2+7^2+2\times\sqrt{17}\times7\times\cos90^\circ}\\ &=8.124\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}. \end{aligned}$$
here, $\alpha=90^\circ$; $u=\sqrt{17}$; $v=7$. **[Description of Figure 14.3 / Figure-2 of the original]** A on the lower bank; B directly opposite on the upper bank and C to the right. From A, the boat's velocity $v$ along AB, the current's velocity $u$ to the right, and the diagonal resultant $w$ along AC. Between $u$ and $v$ the angle is $\alpha=90^\circ$. The path up to C is longer than AB. ∴ distance travelled, $$AC=wt_2$$ $$AC = (8.124\times193.950)\ \mathrm m$$ $$AC = 1575.650\ \mathrm m.$$ it is seen that $AC>AB$. Therefore, to cross the river in the minimum time the boatman must cover a distance greater than the width of the river. questions.stem: The driver of a car moving eastwards at $40\text{ km}$ per hour saw a truck moving northwards at twice his speed per hour. The east direction is taken as the positive $x$-axis and the north direction as the positive $y$-axis.

parts.answer: Let the truck have been moving towards the north-east with velocity $v_T$ at an angle $\theta$ with the north direction.

parts.prompt: Analyse mathematically and show whether it is possible to determine a vector along the direction perpendicular to the plane in which the actual velocities of the truck and the car lie.
parts.answer:
In this case, taking the east direction as the $X$-axis and the north direction as the $Y$-axis, The actual velocity of the car, from $v_c = 40\text{ km/h}$ we get, Velocity vector of the car, $\vec{v}_c = 40\hat{i}\text{ km/h}$ Again, the actual velocity of the truck, $v_T = 40\sqrt{5}\text{ km/h}$, acting on the east side at an angle $26.57^\circ$ with the north direction— Velocity vector of the truck, $\vec{v}_T = (40\sqrt{5}\sin 26.57^\circ)\hat{i} + (40\sqrt{5}\cos 26.57^\circ)\hat{j} = (40\hat{i} + 80\hat{j})\text{ km/h}$ Now, $\vec{v}_c \times \vec{v}_T$ is a vector perpendicular to the plane of $\vec{v}_c$ and $\vec{v}_T$,
$$\therefore \vec{v}_c \times \vec{v}_T = \left|\begin{matrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 40 & 0 & 0 \\ 40 & 80 & 0 \end{matrix}\right| = \hat{i} \times 0 - \hat{j} \times 0 + \hat{k}(40 \times 80 - 0) = 3200\hat{k}$$ Let the unit vector along the direction perpendicular to the plane in which $\vec{v}_c$ and $\vec{v}_T$ lie be = $\hat{\eta}$
$$\therefore \hat{\eta} = \frac{\vec{v}_c \times \vec{v}_T}{|\vec{v}_c \times \vec{v}_T|}$$

$$\hat{\eta} = \frac{3200\hat{k}}{\sqrt{(3200)^2}}$$

$$\hat{\eta} = \hat{k}$$ Therefore it is possible to determine a vector along the direction perpendicular to the plane in which the actual velocities of the truck and the car lie.

parts.prompt: Give your opinion, through mathematical analysis, on whether $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ can be adjacent sides of a parallelogram.
parts.answer:
For two vectors to be adjacent sides of a parallelogram, the two vectors must be non-zero and non-collinear. Determining the magnitudes of the two vectors
$$|\vec{A}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 2^2 + (-1)^2}$$

$$|\vec{A}| = 3$$
$$|\vec{B}| = \sqrt{6^2 + (-3)^2 + 2^2}$$

$$|\vec{B}| = \sqrt{36 + 9 + 4}$$

$$|\vec{B}| = \sqrt{49}$$

$$|\vec{B}| = 7$$
 or, given,
$\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$
$\vec{B} = 6\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$
 Since $|\vec{A}| \neq 0$ and $|\vec{B}| \neq 0$, therefore the two vectors are non-zero. If the two vectors are collinear, then $\vec{A} = k\vec{B}$, where $k$ is a scalar quantity. The two vectors will be collinear if the ratios of the components of $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are equal. Now, the ratio of the $\hat{i}$ component: $\frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$, ratio of the $\hat{j}$ component: $\frac{2}{-3} = -\frac{2}{3}$, ratio of the $\hat{k}$ component: $\frac{-1}{2} = -\frac{1}{2}$ From $\frac{2}{6} \neq \frac{2}{-3} \neq \frac{-1}{2}$ we get, Therefore, the vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are not collinear. Since the two vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are non-zero and non-collinear, they can represent two adjacent sides of a parallelogram. Therefore, a parallelogram can be formed with the two vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$.

parts.prompt: Do the two vectors obey the commutative law of vector multiplication? Analyse mathematically. (4)**

Using the value of $m$ obtained from part (c) we get, First vector, $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}$ Second vector, $\vec{B} = -28\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 10\hat{k}$ According to the commutative law of vector multiplication, $\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \vec{B} \times \vec{A}$ `[assumed for verification]`
$$\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \left|\begin{matrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 3 & -5 \\ -28 & 2 & -10 \end{matrix}\right|$$
$$\text{or, } \vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \hat{i}\{3(-10) - (-5)2\} - \hat{j}\{2(-10) - (-5)(-28)\} + \hat{k}\{2(2) - 3(-28)\}$$
$$\text{or, } \vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \hat{i}(-30 + 10) - \hat{j}(-20 - 140) + \hat{k}(4 + 84)$$
$$\therefore \vec{A} \times \vec{B} = -20\hat{i} + 160\hat{j} + 88\hat{k}$$
$$\vec{B} \times \vec{A} = \left|\begin{matrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ -28 & 2 & -10 \\ 2 & 3 & -5 \end{matrix}\right|$$
$$\hat{i}\{2(-5) - (-10)3\} - \hat{j}\{(-28)(-5) - (-10)2\} + \hat{k}\{(-28)3 - 2(2)\}$$
$$\hat{i}(-10 + 30) - \hat{j}(140 + 20) + \hat{k}(-84 - 4)$$
$$\therefore \vec{B} \times \vec{A} = 20\hat{i} - 160\hat{j} - 88\hat{k}$$
$$\vec{B} \times \vec{A} = -(-20\hat{i} + 160\hat{j} + 88\hat{k})$$

$$\vec{B} \times \vec{A} = -(\vec{A} \times \vec{B})$$ it is seen that $\vec{A} \times \vec{B} \neq \vec{B} \times \vec{A}$. Therefore it can be said that the two vectors do not obey the commutative law of vector multiplication.

$$\overrightarrow{PQ}=(-2-4)\hat i+(4+2)\hat j+(5-3)\hat k$$ $$\overrightarrow{PQ} = -6\hat i+6\hat j+2\hat k$$ $$\overrightarrow{QR}=(-1+2)\hat i+(2-4)\hat j+(-2-5)\hat k$$ $$\overrightarrow{QR} = \hat i-2\hat j-7\hat k.$$ Here, the three points—P(4, −2, 3), Q(−2, 4, 5), R(−1, 2, −2).
$$\begin{aligned} \overrightarrow{PQ}\times\overrightarrow{QR} &=\left|\begin{matrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\-6&6&2\\1&-2&-7\end{matrix}\right|\\ &=\hat i[\{6\times(-7)\}-\{2\times(-2)\}]-\hat j[\{(-6)\times(-7)\}-\{2\times1\}]+\hat k[\{(-6)\times(-2)\}-\{6\times1\}]. \end{aligned}$$
*The rest of this answer is in Image 03 / page 31.* * * * # Image 03 — printed page 31 Source: `split_page32-75-03.png` ## Remaining part of the answer to Question 3 **(c). (continuing)** $$\overrightarrow{PQ}\times\overrightarrow{QR}=-38\hat i-40\hat j+6\hat k$$ $$\therefore\left|\overrightarrow{PQ}\times\overrightarrow{QR}\right|=\sqrt{(-38)^2+(-40)^2+6^2}=2\sqrt{770}.$$ that is, the unit vector of $\overrightarrow{PQ}\times\overrightarrow{QR}$

parts.prompt: Will the three points in the stem form a right-angled triangle? Analyse mathematically.
parts.answer:
From (c) we get,

$$\overrightarrow{PQ}=-6\hat i+6\hat j+2\hat k,$$
$$\overrightarrow{QR}=\hat i-2\hat j-7\hat k.$$
 Now,

$$\overrightarrow{PR}=(-1-4)\hat i+(2+2)\hat j+(-2-3)\hat k$$

$$\overrightarrow{PR} = -5\hat i+4\hat j-\hat k$$

$$|\overrightarrow{PQ}|=\sqrt{(-6)^2+6^2+2^2}$$

$$|\overrightarrow{PQ}| = 2\sqrt{19}$$
$$|\overrightarrow{QR}|=\sqrt{1^2+(-2)^2+(-7)^2}$$

$$|\overrightarrow{QR}| = 3\sqrt6$$
$$|\overrightarrow{PR}|=\sqrt{(-5)^2+4^2+(-1)^2}$$

$$|\overrightarrow{PR}| = \sqrt{42}.$$
 Here, three points: P(4, −2, 3), Q(−2, 4, 5), R(−1, 2, −2).
 Now,

$$|\overrightarrow{QR}|^2+|\overrightarrow{PR}|^2=(3\sqrt6)^2+(\sqrt{42})^2=96$$
 and

$$|\overrightarrow{PQ}|^2=(2\sqrt{19})^2$$

$$|\overrightarrow{PQ}|^2 = 76.$$

$$\therefore|\overrightarrow{PQ}|^2\ne|\overrightarrow{QR}|^2+|\overrightarrow{PR}|^2.$$
 ∴ the three points in the stem do not form a right-angled triangle.
 In the z-component of the original's calculation of $\overrightarrow{PR}$, `(-2−3)` is written but the result is printed as `−1`. Correct $\overrightarrow{PR}=-5\hat i+4\hat j-5\hat k$ and $|\overrightarrow{PR}|=\sqrt{66}$. The squares of the three sides are 76, 54, 66; no two of them add up to the third. Hence the conclusion 'not right-angled' is correct, but the intermediate calculation is wrong. The original answer also shows only one inequality without checking the longest side.

$$\therefore |\vec{d_1} \times \vec{d_2}| = 16.97$$ Area of the parallelogram with the help of the diagonal, $A = \frac{1}{2}|\vec{d_1} \times \vec{d_2}|$

parts.prompt: Will that person's plan succeed or not — analyse mathematically.

The scalar triple product of the three vectors $\vec{A}$, $\vec{B}$ and $\vec{C}$,
$$\vec{A} \cdot (\vec{B} \times \vec{C}) = \left|\begin{matrix} 3 & -4 & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \end{matrix}\right|$$
$$\text{or, } \vec{A} \cdot (\vec{B} \times \vec{C}) = 3((-1)(-3) - (1)(2)) - ((-4)(2)(-3) - (1)(1)) + 5((2)(2) - (-1)(1))$$

$$\text{or, } \vec{A} \cdot (\vec{B} \times \vec{C}) = 3(3 - 2) + 4(-6 - 1) + 5(4 + 1) = 3(1) + 4(-7) + 5(5) = 28 - 28$$

$\vec{B} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$
$\vec{C} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$

according to the stem,
$$\vec{P} + \vec{Q} + \vec{R} = 0$$
$$\text{or, } \vec{P} = -(\vec{Q} + \vec{R})$$ Squaring both sides we get,
$$|\vec{P}|^2 = |-(\vec{Q} + \vec{R})|^2$$
$$\text{or, } P^2 = |(\vec{Q} + \vec{R})|^2$$
$$\text{or, } P^2 = Q^2 + R^2 + 2\vec{Q} \cdot \vec{R}$$
$$\text{or, } 3^2 = 4^2 + 5^2 + 2(\vec{Q} \cdot \vec{R})$$
$$\text{or, } 9 = 41 + 2(\vec{Q} \cdot \vec{R})$$
$$\text{or, } 2(\vec{Q} \cdot \vec{R}) = 9 - 41$$

$$\text{or, } 2(\vec{Q} \cdot \vec{R}) = -32$$

parts.prompt: Can the value of $\vec{R} \times (\vec{P} \times \vec{Q})$ be determined? Analyse mathematically.
parts.answer:
According to the stem, the magnitudes of the vectors $\vec{P}, \vec{Q}$ and $\vec{R}$ are $3, 4$ and $5$ respectively. Here, $P^2 + Q^2 = 3^2 + 4^2 = 25 = 5^2 = R^2$. Since Pythagoras' theorem is satisfied, the angle between $P$ and $Q$ is $90^\circ$ (because they form a right-angled triangle in which the resultant is the hypotenuse). We know,
$$|\vec{P} \times \vec{Q}| = PQ\sin 90^\circ$$

$$|\vec{P} \times \vec{Q}| = 3 \times 4 \times 1$$

$$|\vec{P} \times \vec{Q}| = 12$$ This new vector will act perpendicular to the plane in which $P$ and $Q$ lie. Again, since $\vec{P}, \vec{Q}, \vec{R}$ lie in the same plane (because their sum is zero), the vector $\vec{R}$ will remain perpendicular (at an angle $90^\circ$) to the vector $(\vec{P} \times \vec{Q})$.
**Answer:** $|\vec{R} \times (\vec{P} \times \vec{Q})| = R \cdot |\vec{P} \times \vec{Q}| \cdot \sin 90^\circ = 5 \times 12 \times 1 = 60$ Therefore, through mathematical analysis it is seen that the value of $R \times (P \times Q)$ can be determined and its value is $60$.

parts.prompt: Can a rectangular solid be made from the three vectors in the stem? Analyse mathematically.

A rectangular solid can be made from three vectors only when the three vectors are mutually perpendicular. If the three vectors are mutually perpendicular, the dot product of any two of them will be zero.

$$\vec A\cdot\vec C=(2)(1)+(1)(3)+(3)(2)$$

 since $\vec A\cdot\vec C\ne0$, therefore $\vec A$ and $\vec C$ are not mutually perpendicular.
 Since no pair of the three vectors is mutually perpendicular, therefore a rectangular solid cannot be made from the three vectors of the stem.

parts.prompt: Determine the value of $\vec{\nabla}\left(\frac{1}{r}\right)$.

 Now,
$$\vec{\nabla} \times \vec{V} = \left|\begin{matrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ V_x & V_y & V_z \end{matrix}\right|$$ coefficient of $\hat{i}$ = $\frac{\partial V_z}{\partial y} - \frac{\partial V_y}{\partial z} = \frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(\frac{z}{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}\right) - \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(\frac{y}{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}\right)$ or, $\frac{\partial V_z}{\partial y} - \frac{\partial V_y}{\partial z} = z\left(-\frac{2y}{(x^2 + y^2 + z^2)^2}\right) - y\left(-\frac{2z}{(x^2 + y^2 + z^2)^2}\right)$
$\therefore \frac{\partial V_z}{\partial y} - \frac{\partial V_y}{\partial z} = -\frac{2yz}{r^4} + \frac{2yz}{r^4} = 0$ Similarly it is seen that the coefficients of $\hat{j}$ and $\hat{k}$ will also be zero.
$$\frac{\partial V_x}{\partial z} - \frac{\partial V_z}{\partial x} = 0$$
$$\text{and, } \frac{\partial V_y}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial V_x}{\partial y} = 0$$
$$\therefore \vec{\nabla} \times \left(\frac{\vec{r}}{r^2}\right) = 0\hat{i} + 0\hat{j} + 0\hat{k} = \vec{0}$$ Since a vector field is irrotational when its curl is zero, and since the value of $\vec{\nabla} \times \left(\frac{\vec{r}}{r^2}\right)$ in the stem is zero, it is an irrotational vector.

questions.stem:
A bus, a jeep and a truck are moving along a road. Their velocities are respectively — $\vec{v_1} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k},\; \vec{v_2} = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ and $\vec{v_3} = \hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$. At some instant a collision occurs among the three.

*This question has no figure (quantity/definition based only).*

parts.prompt: Determine the curl of the velocity of the truck.
parts.answer:
Given, $\text{Curl}(\vec{v_3}) = \vec{\nabla} \times \vec{v_3}$
$$\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\hat{i} + \frac{\partial}{\partial y}\hat{j} + \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\hat{k}\right) \times (\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 5\hat{k})$$
$$\left|\begin{matrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ 1 & -3 & 5 \end{matrix}\right|$$
$$\hat{i}\left\{\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(5) - \frac{\partial}{\partial z}(-3)\right\} - \hat{j}\left\{\frac{\partial}{\partial z}(5) - \frac{\partial}{\partial x}(1)\right\} + \hat{k}\left\{\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(-3) - \frac{\partial}{\partial y}(1)\right\}$$
$$\hat{i}(0 - 0) - \hat{j}(0 - 0) + \hat{k}(0 - 0)$$ $$\therefore \text{Curl}(\vec{v_3}) = 0\text{ Ans.}$$

parts.prompt: Prove mathematically that at the moment of collision the three vehicles were moving in the same plane.
parts.answer:
The three vectors will lie in the same plane if $(\vec{v_1} \times \vec{v_2}) \cdot \vec{v_3} = 0$. here, $(\vec{v_1} \times \vec{v_2}) = (2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}) \times (3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})$
$$\left|\begin{matrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & -2 & 4 \end{matrix}\right| = (4 - 2)\hat{i} - (8 + 3)\hat{j} + (-4 - 3)\hat{k} = 2\hat{i} - 11\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}$$ Since $(\vec{v_1} \times \vec{v_2}) \cdot \vec{v_3} = (2\hat{i} - 11\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}) \cdot (\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}) = 2 + 33 - 35 = 0$
$$\therefore (\vec{v_1} \times \vec{v_2}) \cdot \vec{v_3} = 0$$ Since $(\vec{v_1} \times \vec{v_2}) \cdot \vec{v_3} = 0$, therefore the three vectors lie in the same plane. Therefore, at the moment of collision the three vehicles were moving in the same plane.

questions.stem: According to the figure, three forces are applied on a stationary particle at point $O$.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the resultant force acting on the particle along $OX$.
parts.answer:
Let the resultant force $\vec{F}$ make an angle $\theta$ with the direction of $OX$. the angle of $\vec{F}_1$ with $OX$, $\theta_1 = 0^\circ$ the angle of $\vec{F}_2$ with $OX$, $\theta_2 = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ$ the angle of $\vec{F}_3$ with $OX$, $\theta_3 = 270^\circ - 30^\circ = 240^\circ$
$\therefore$ the magnitude of the resultant force acting on the particle along $OX$,
$$F_x = |\vec{F}|\cos\theta$$

$$F_x = |\vec{F}_1|\cos\theta_1 + |\vec{F}_2|\cos\theta_2 + |\vec{F}_3|\cos\theta_3$$
$$F_x = 11\cos 0^\circ + 22\cos 120^\circ + 33\cos 240^\circ$$
$$-16.5\text{ N Ans.}$$

parts.prompt: In which direction will the particle move as a result of the applied force? Give your opinion with mathematical analysis.
parts.answer:
Obtained from (c), $F_x=-16.5\ \mathrm N\quad\cdots(i)$. similarly,
$$\begin{aligned} F_y&=|\vec F|\sin\theta=|\vec F_1|\sin\theta_1+|\vec F_2|\sin\theta_2+|\vec F_3|\sin\theta_3\\ &=11\sin0^\circ+22\sin120^\circ+33\sin240^\circ\\ &=-\frac{11\sqrt3}{2}\ \mathrm N\quad\cdots(ii). \end{aligned}$$
here, $|\vec F_1|=11\ \mathrm N$; $|\vec F_2|=22\ \mathrm N$; $|\vec F_3|=33\ \mathrm N$. Dividing (ii) by (i) we get, $$\frac{F_x}{F_y}=\frac{|\vec F|\sin\theta}{|\vec F|\cos\theta}$$ $$\frac{F_x}{F_y} = \frac{-\frac{11\sqrt3}{2}}{-16.5}.\quad\text{[left-hand side of the original]}$$ or, $$\tan\theta=\frac1{\sqrt3}$$ $$\therefore\theta=210^\circ.$$ (Since $\sin\theta$, both $\cos\theta$ are negative, so $\theta$ lies in the 3rd quadrant.) Therefore, as a result of the applied force the particle will move at an angle of 210° with the direction of OX; in other words, at an angle of (210° − 180°) = 30° downwards with the direction of OX′. On the division line the left-hand side is printed as $F_x/F_y$, but according to the right-hand side and the division indicated it should be $F_y/F_x$. The angle 210° and the magnitudes of both components are correct. In (c) by 'magnitude' the signed component −16.5 N is meant; the absolute value is 16.5 N, direction OX′.

questions.source: Barishal Board · 2023 · Board question no. 1 · book p. 48
questions.stem: Nahin and Jahin were dragging a heavy stationary truck by tying two ropes to it. An angle of '$\alpha$' is created between the two ropes. The truck was moving towards Nahin. Nahin told Jahin to apply more force.

parts.prompt: Show that if Jahin applies a force equal in magnitude to Nahin's, their resultant force will bisect the angle between them.
parts.answer:
Let the forces applied by Jahin and Nahin be $P$ and $Q$ respectively, the angle between the two forces $\alpha$ and the resultant $R$. If the resultant $R$ acts at an angle $\theta$ with $P$, then
$$\tan\theta = \frac{Q\sin\alpha}{P + Q\cos\alpha}$$ If Jahin applies a force equal to Nahin's then $P = Q$
$$\therefore \tan\theta = \frac{Q\sin\alpha}{Q + Q\cos\alpha}$$
$$\text{or, } \tan\theta = \frac{Q\sin\alpha}{Q(1 + \cos\alpha)}$$

$$\text{or, } \tan\theta = \frac{\sin\alpha}{1 + \cos\alpha}$$

$$\text{or, } \tan\theta = \frac{2\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}}{2\cos^2\frac{\alpha}{2}}$$

$$\text{or, } \tan\theta = \frac{\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}}{\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}}$$
$$\therefore \tan\theta = \tan\frac{\alpha}{2}$$
$$\theta = \frac{\alpha}{2}$$ Therefore, their resultant force will bisect the angle between them. (Shown)

questions.stem:
**Scenario-1:** In the laboratory, a slide calliper was used to measure the diameter of a solid cylinder. The main-scale reading was $4.2\text{ cm}$ and the vernier coincidence was $8$. The vernier constant of the instrument is $0.01\text{cm}$. The cylinder is rolling down an inclined plane.

**Scenario-2:** While the cylinder is rotating, its angular velocity vector is $\vec{\omega} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}\text{ rad/s}$ and its radius vector is $\vec{r} = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}\text{ m}$.

*This question has no figure (quantity/definition based only).*

parts.prompt: Determine the diameter of the cylinder in Scenario-1 and find the relative error in determining the volume (assume the height is error-free $10\text{ cm}$).
parts.answer:
We know,
$$\text{diameter, } D = M + V \times VC$$

$$\text{diameter, } D = 4.2 + 8 \times 0.01$$

$$\text{diameter, } D = 4.2 + 0.08$$

$$\text{diameter, } D = 4.28\text{ cm}$$
 In the case of a slide calliper the final error in measurement is equal to the vernier constant. Final error in the diameter measurement, $\Delta D = VC = 0.01\text{ cm}$ Diameter of the cylinder, $D = 4.28\text{ cm}$, height of the cylinder, $h = 10\text{ cm}$ Actual volume of the cylinder,
$$V = \frac{\pi}{4} D^2 h$$

$$V = \frac{\pi}{4} \times (4.28)^2 \times 10$$

$$V = 143.87\text{ cm}^3$$ Maximum value in the diameter measurement, $D_{\max} = D + \Delta D = 4.28 + 0.01 = 4.29\text{ cm}$ Maximum volume of the cylinder,
$$V_{\max} = \frac{\pi}{4} D_{\max}^2 h$$

$$V_{\max} = \frac{\pi}{4} \times (4.29)^2 \times 10$$

$$V_{\max} = 144.54\text{ cm}^3$$ Minimum value in the diameter measurement, $D_{\min} = D - \Delta D = 4.28 - 0.01 = 4.27\text{ cm}$ Minimum volume of the cylinder,
$$V_{\min} = \frac{\pi}{4} D_{\min}^2 h$$

$$V_{\min} = \frac{\pi}{4} \times (4.27)^2 \times 10$$

$$V_{\min} = 143.2\text{ cm}^3$$ Final error for the maximum volume, $\Delta V_1 = |V_{\max} - V| = |144.54 - 143.87| = 0.67\text{ cm}^3$ Final error for the minimum volume, $\Delta V_2 = |V_{\min} - V| = |143.2 - 143.87| = 0.67\text{ cm}^3$ Final error in measuring the volume of the cube `[cylinder]`, $\Delta V = 0.67\text{ cm}^3$ Relative error in determining the volume of the cube `[cylinder]`, $\frac{\Delta V}{V} = \frac{0.67}{143.87} = 0.00465$ Percentage relative error = $0.00465 \times 100\% = 0.465\%$ Ans.

parts.prompt: In the light of the information in Scenario-2, determine the linear velocity vector of the cylinder and show that the linear velocity is perpendicular to the radius vector.
parts.answer:
We know, Linear velocity vector,
$$\vec{v} = \vec{\omega} \times \vec{r}$$

$$\vec{v} = (2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}) \times (\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})$$
$$\left|\begin{matrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \end{matrix}\right| = (-6 + 2)\hat{i} - (4 - 1)\hat{j} + (-4 + 3)\hat{k}$$
$$\therefore \vec{v} = -4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}\text{ ms}^{-1}$$
 Again, two vectors will be mutually perpendicular if their dot product is zero. Here, for $\vec{v} = -4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{r} = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$, now, $\vec{v} \cdot \vec{r} = (-4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}) \cdot (\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) = -4 + 6 - 2 = 0$ Since the dot product of the linear velocity vector $\vec{v}$ and the radius vector $\vec{r}$ is zero, therefore the linear velocity vector is perpendicular to the radius vector.

questions.source: BCIC College, Dhaka · Board question no. 5 · book p. 62
questions.stem:
Three marbles — black, blue and red — on a flat table are set moving with velocities $\vec{v_1} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$, $\vec{v_2} = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$ and $\vec{v_3} = \hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$ respectively, and a collision occurs between them.

*This question has no figure (quantity/definition based only).*

parts.prompt: After the collision the red marble was at rest. Explain according to the stem.
parts.answer:
We know that the impulse of a force applied on a body ($\vec{j}$) is equal to the change in the momentum of the body. impulse of the force,
$$\vec{j} = \Delta\vec{P_3}$$

$$\vec{j} = \vec{P_3}' - \vec{P_3}$$
$$\text{or, } \vec{j} = m_3\vec{v_3}' - m_3\vec{v_3}$$
$$\text{or, } \vec{j} = m_3(0) - m_3(\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 5\hat{k})$$
$$\text{or, } \vec{j} = -m_3\hat{i} + 3m_3\hat{j} - 5m_3\hat{k}$$ 
 After the collision the red marble was at rest, i.e. its final velocity is zero ($\vec{v_3}' = 0$). This means that the impulse ($\vec{j}$) applied to the red marble by the other two marbles (black and blue) during the collision was equal in magnitude to the red marble's initial momentum ($\vec{P_3}$) and opposite in direction to that initial momentum. Initial momentum, $\vec{P_3} = m_3(\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 5\hat{k})$. Then the impulse of the force, $\vec{j} = -\vec{P_3}$. Therefore, as a result of the collision the red marble receives an impulse equal and opposite to its initial momentum, so that the velocity of the marble becomes zero and it comes to rest.

> [book printing error: -5m₃ĵ is printed at the end, which should be -5m₃k̂]

parts.prompt: Is there a possibility that the marbles stay on the flat table after the collision? Explain with analysis.
parts.answer:
Whether the marbles were moving on the flat table depends on whether their velocity vectors lie in the same plane. If the three velocity vectors ($\vec{v_1}, \vec{v_2}, \vec{v_3}$) are coplanar, their scalar triple product will be zero. Given, the velocity of the black marble $\vec{v_1} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$, the velocity of the blue marble $\vec{v_2} = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$ and the velocity of the red marble $\vec{v_3} = \hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$ then,
$$\text{here, } (\vec{v_1} \times \vec{v_2}) \cdot \vec{v_3} = \left|\begin{matrix} 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & -2 & -4 \\ 1 & -3 & 5 \end{matrix}\right|$$
$$2(-10 - 12) - 1(15 + 4) - 1(-9 + 2) = -44 - 19 + 7$$

$$2(-10 - 12) - 1(15 + 4) - 1(-9 + 2) = -56$$ Since the scalar triple product is not zero, i.e. $(\vec{v_1} \times \vec{v_2}) \cdot \vec{v_3} = -56 \neq 0$, therefore the initial velocity vectors of the three marbles are not coplanar. Since the initial velocity vectors are not coplanar, their motion is three-dimensional. Even after the collision, according to the law of conservation of momentum, their motion will remain three-dimensional. Therefore, there is no possibility that the marbles will stay on the flat table after the collision.
